A reference-safe result for fixed-support coherent release

There is a useful consequence for an arbitrary CPTP release channel supported on a fixed physical set  $F$ .

Start with a thermal syndrome marginal. Let  $U_F$  be the subspace of syndrome shifts generated by Paulis supported on  $F$ . A Kraus operator on  $F$  connects an input syndrome only to syndromes in that coset. Complete positivity and trace preservation therefore give

 $\mu_F(b)
\le
\sum_{u\in U_F}\pi(b+u)
\le
\left[4e^{\beta c_E}\right]^{|F|}\pi(b).$ This does not replace coherent Kraus operators with a stochastic Pauli mixture. Logical/reference correlations remain present.

Stationarity, positivity, and the accepted complete logical-hazard reduction imply

 $\mathrm{error}(t)
\le
\mathrm{initial\ decoded\ error}
+
2t\left[4e^{\beta c_E}\right]^{|F|}\pi(h).$ For a fixed localized release, this transfers the equilibrium suppression to the subsequent physical evolution.

It does not cover the actual constant-density release regime. Even an independent positive-density pulse makes the naive averaged prefactor exponential in  $N$ ; the general  $p$ -bounded law may additionally correlate with earlier records. The missing result must control the faults connected to a dangerous decoded witness while allowing the exterior to evolve under the real bath.

I also examined Baspin’s free-energy-flow framework as a possible way to improve the correction-path comparison. That source supplies a framework for thermalization bounds; I did not construct the required BDL flow or derive noisy-release retention from it. arxiv.org [https://arxiv.org/html/2509.17356v1?utm_source=chatgpt.com]
